thread:
incident-bot: P0 alert — high 5xx rate observed from euc3 cluster (service=ingress) at 2026-03-15T20:12:47Z. Rule: ALB/NLB_5xx_rate > 2.5% for 5m. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/INC-2401
carla: paging on-call @mike-sre @sunita. customers seeing failed generations and timeouts. :rotating_light:
mike-sre: on-call here, pulling up Grafana and NLB metrics now.
sunita: joining. any sign it's an application regression or infra?
carlos-support: 4 customer tickets in last 8m for /v1/chat and /v1/generate returning 502/504s (org-a, org-rt, payment-co, newsinc). customers reporting retries succeeding sometimes.
mike-sre: Envoy logs show: 
```
[2026-03-15T20:12:40Z] envoy upstream reset: connection reset by peer, 502
[2026-03-15T20:12:41Z] upstream response timeout
```
Looks like upstream NLB or instance NIC issue.
raj-platform: AWS console shows target-group nlb-euc3b-ingress with a spike in UnhealthyHostCount and high health check latency starting 2026-03-15T20:11:30Z. Instance-level metrics show ENI RxErrors rising.
carla: runbook step 1: confirm target health and consider temporary AZ failover. I'm notifying platform lead.
carla: @raj-platform — can you confirm if there's any scheduled infra work?
raj-platform: no scheduled maintenance. I'm checking instance syslogs and dmesg for ENI errors. Also opening cloud provider support case.
mike-sre: short mitigation plan: (A) mark affected targets OutOfService in target group to stop sending traffic to euc3b, (B) restart envoy pods in euc3b if necessary, (C) capture pcaps and metrics.
sunita: agree. if NLB is flapping, prefer targeted OutOfService toggles to avoid cascading GC on other AZs.
carla: executing toggle for 3 targets in nlb-euc3b-ingress now. will monitor error rate.
carla: toggled targets to OutOfService at 2026-03-15T20:13:22Z.
eng-sre-bot: automation: scheduled rolling restart for envoy-ingress-euc3b deployment initiated by mike-sre.
mike-sre: kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/envoy-ingress-euc3b  # rolling restart to refresh upstream connections
mike-sre: running quick healthcheck: curl -sS -D - https://ingress-euc3b.internal/health | head -n 20 — seeing intermittent connection resets locally.
sunita: collecting tcpdump on node eni-10.2.50.1: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/euc3b_ingress.pcap 'tcp and port 443'
raj-platform: kernel logs show `rx_ring_overruns` and `tx_dma_timeout` messages around 20:11:50Z. hypothesis: NIC firmware or driver regression causing packet drops and RSTs.
carlos-support: customer-facing note: partial degradation between 20:11 and 20:16 UTC; some requests returned 5xx, recommending client retries with backoff. Support leads notified.
carla: error rate dropped from 5.2% to 0.7% ~90s after toggling. Looks mitigated for now.
mike-sre: leaving euc3b targets out for 20 minutes while we investigate. Do not re-enable until cloud support confirms NIC/instance health.
sunita: for RCA we need: pcaps, dmesg, instance metrics (ENI errors, NIC drops), NLB health timeline, health check logs, NAT gateway metrics for subnet. Also check ephemeral port allocation on workers.
raj-platform: I've attached packet capture to cloud case and referenced possible large-seg/offload interaction. Raised case ID AWS-CASE-2026-34721.
carla: creating incident ticket INC-2401 on status page. severity: degraded (user impact) — P0 alert but mitigated by failover, P1 for RCA. ETA: RCA draft due in 72h.
mike-sre: next actions: (1) leave failover in place until cloud support responds, (2) collect all artifacts and upload to incident ticket, (3) coordinate with infra to consider instance replacement or NIC firmware rollback if confirmed.
eng-sre-bot: note: auto-sampler collected 10s of heap profiles from envoy pods at 20:14:00Z.
sunita: capturing metrics snapshot: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name NetworkPacketsOut ...` and saving to /var/tmp/incident_metrics_euc3b.json
carla: customer comms sent and updated status: partial outage, mitigation applied, investigating.
raj-platform: cloud support responded: they can see NIC driver errors on host hypervisor for our instances in euc3b and recommend moving traffic off those hosts and replacing instances; they've requested additional pcaps and kernel logs.
carla: handoff: @mike-sre will monitor for next 30m, then @sunita will own RCA and write postmortem. tagging @oncall-next for midnight handover.
mike-sre: monitoring — 5xxs at ~0.4% and trending down. No new customer reports in 12m.
sunita: starting timeline reconstruction: 20:11:10Z health checks start to lag, 20:11:30Z target states unhealthy spike, 20:13:20Z failover toggles applied, 20:14:50Z 5xxs sub-1%.
carlos-support: confirming affected customers informed; recorded incident window 20:110:16 UTC for their tickets.
carla: incident status: MITIGATED (temporary failover). Postmortem owner: sunita; action items: review NIC driver, add better health-check thresholds for ingress, and add automated cross-AZ failover doc.
incident-bot: INC-2401 status changed to MITIGATED by carla. Postmortem due in 72 hours.
mike-sre: note: do not re-add euc3b targets until we have instance replacement or cloud confirms fix. tag runbook flag "await-cloud-nic-fix".
sunita: copying artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2401/artifacts/ (pcap, metrics, logs). Will draft RCA with hypothesis: NIC driver regression causing packet drops and upstream RSTs; alternate hypothesis: NAT gateway overload causing return-path drops.
carlos-support: thanks team. I'll follow up with customers after RCA.
carla: closing active responder channel; leave thread open for RCA comments. great triage and quick mitigation. :white_check_mark:
